content.text: I fixed the bug in `solution/core.py`, and the visible suite now passes (3 tests). The binary operators (ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD, EQ, LT, GT) popped their operands in the wrong order. The code did `a, b = pop(), pop()`, which made `a` the top of the stack, but the left operand is the one pushed first. That made `LT`, `GT`, `SUB`, `DIV` and `MOD` compute with the operands swapped. It also explains the other two failures. With `1 0 DIV` the divisor was read as 1, so no `VMZeroDivision` was raised. The countdown loop computed `1 - n` instead of `n - 1`, so it never reached zero and hit the step limit. The fix changes that line to `b, a = pop(), pop()`.

result: I fixed the bug in `solution/core.py`, and the visible suite now passes (3 tests). The binary operators (ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD, EQ, LT, GT) popped their operands in the wrong order. The code did `a, b = pop(), pop()`, which made `a` the top of the stack, but the left operand is the one pushed first. That made `LT`, `GT`, `SUB`, `DIV` and `MOD` compute with the operands swapped. It also explains the other two failures. With `1 0 DIV` the divisor was read as 1, so no `VMZeroDivision` was raised. The countdown loop computed `1 - n` instead of `n - 1`, so it never reached zero and hit the step limit. The fix changes that line to `b, a = pop(), pop()`.
